posts.author: Bobson
posts.body:
Hello all!
First off, I'd like to apologize in advance if this has been answered multiple times already. I've tried searching for a relevant thread in the forums but had limited success.
Second, I've just started on my journey using RPG Maker MZ and I don't have much experience in coding, design and all that. Basically, I'm learning as I go and I'm using vanilla assets.
With that out of the way, I used the built-in character generator and was able to make the character face portraits, battler animation, etc. and have successfully applied these generated characters to my actors. But when I went to view their full portraits on the menu, it doesn't match the face portrait that have been assigned to the actor and it looks like it's displaying the default portraits. I noticed that aside from the face portrait, there is also another folder named "pictures" and it looks like the default full character portrait is supposed to be saved there. But I see no option to export a full character portrait on the character generator.
Is there a way to be able to generate and export full character portraits without the use of plugins? Or, I might be missing something obvious but I'm just blind to it. If there really is no option but to use plugins, I'd appreciate it if you can recommend a plugin (links if possible) that I can use for this.
Thank you in advance for all the help!

posts.author: Avery
posts.body:
Simple answer: No.
The good thing is that several of the generator options are similar to the option of the default characters, so you often can edit something matching your generated char out of them: but that is actual manual artistic work.
Doable, but it takes some time and can be a bit fiddly.
Bust Edits for Beginners | The Official RPG Maker Blog
The character generator has come a long way… do you remember the haunting results of the VX Ace generator faces? But even now, with MZ, even though the results look pretty good, you might want something a bit more special for an important character. Let's learn how to make quick edits using...
www.rpgmakerweb.com
Something to keep in mind is that in a generator, each body shape and pose would require all of the assets being tailored to them, so all results would look quite stiff and uniform sharing the same base - and it is just a lot of work. The generator files in general are already super time consuming to make and set up anyways.
